baseline: BENCHMARK VERSION 1. This is a synthetic, cumulative target-design exercise, not a deployed system or an account of Atlassian's implementation. Build a new agent-assisted customer service and field service SaaS product on Microsoft Azure. Confirmed constraints: the provider operates one Azure subscription per customer, with dedicated application, transactional data, search, and agent runtime resources; a shared provider management layer operates the fleet. Customers are US Fortune 500 organizations and smaller businesses with 100–1,200 customer-service staff. Customer business data stays in US regions. Dedicated resources must not be replaced with a shared customer data plane in later stages. Synthetic test assumptions, not customer commitments: enterprise SSO initially uses customer Microsoft Entra ID directories; provider workforce identity is separate; other SAML/OIDC providers are a future interface, not an implemented integration. Exclude payment card data, clinical records, regulated decision automation, and autonomous physical equipment control. Ordinary customer contact data and confidential service records are in scope. A security architect must challenge these exclusions if a feature crosses them. Use a neutral, white-paper technical palette, US English, official Azure icons, and no Microsoft endorsement. All packs are explicitly labeled review drafts, accepted for rendering but not production approval. Choose an actual supported US region and service tier only after checking official Microsoft documentation and disclose capacity, quota, cost and availability verification still required. The quality bar is deployment realism: a delivery team must be able to turn the pack into infrastructure and application work without inventing identity boundaries, connectivity, durable state or failure semantics. Every stage must retain the complete cumulative architecture, with a concise change/migration table rather than only an incremental diagram. Stable component IDs and flow numbers persist unless a documented change retires them. Produce every Atlas Azure output, including a real searchable PDF, editable SVG views, canonical JSON, narrative, HTML, palette, icon provenance and a visual verification receipt. Inspect every PDF page and every view. Never substitute a diagram contact sheet or text extraction for visual inspection. Do not provision Azure resources. Proposed SLOs, prices, quotas, backup and failover behavior are not tested results. Do not optimize to a page count at the expense of implementation detail; split crowded views and use progressive explanation for junior developers, CTOs, external enterprise architects and security architects.

stages.title: Human-approved customer service assistance
stages.requirements: Design the first production-shaped customer deployment and the minimum shared provider management foundation. A service representative signs in, opens a case, retrieves authorized knowledge, receives a cited case summary and draft response, edits it and explicitly approves sending. Cases arrive through an authenticated web/API channel; email ingestion is not yet required. Tenant-local ingestion accepts approved documents, preserves source access groups and deletion/version events, and builds a searchable index. Documents are untrusted data, never agent instructions. An agent cannot change entitlements, send messages or invoke business tools without application-side authorization. Synthetic sizing for the largest customer: 1,200 named staff, 600 concurrently signed in, 60 peak case reads/writes per second, 12 AI requests per second, 500,000 cases/year, 100,000 knowledge documents averaging 100 KB. Explain token and concurrency assumptions rather than inferring model capacity from request counts. Initial service target: 99.9% monthly core case availability, p95 ordinary API latency under 800 ms excluding model and external-system time, p95 first AI response within 8 seconds as a target to validate. Single-region zonal resilience where supported; regional disaster restore target RTO 8 hours and RPO 24 hours without claiming hot regional failover. Retain cases 3 years, knowledge according to source lifecycle, and security audit records 1 year; support legal holds and scoped deletion. Management services can deploy resources and see redacted health metadata but cannot routinely read case content, prompts, completions, embeddings or customer secrets. Provider support access is time-bound, approved and audited. Include subscription onboarding, budgets, deployment identity, private data-service access, DNS, controlled outbound model/tool traffic, telemetry, backup and restore ownership. Choose the smallest plausible managed hosting baseline; compare rather than default to Kubernetes. Supply a concrete deployment parameter/setting table and ordered infrastructure/application deployment checklist, including health tests, denied-access tests and rollback. No executable IaC is required by this input; missing provider quota and cloud validation must remain explicit.
acceptance: Show provider Entra identity, customer Entra SSO, application and workload identities, per-customer subscription and dedicated resource placement, nonproduction separation, management-plane/data-plane separation, and a cross-customer denied-access test.

Trace the numbered sign-in, case-read, ingestion, authorization-filtered retrieval, model request, human approval and response-send paths with payloads, protocols, permissions, durable writes and failure behavior. Approval must bind to the exact action/content version sent.

Assess all eight Atlas platform areas. Explain actual ingress, private endpoint/DNS and egress routes, public-access restrictions, inherited policy controls, platform/workload ownership and verification; do not treat a private-endpoint icon as a complete network design.

Specify concrete service/hosting/tier choices, behavior-changing settings, region support evidence, scaling assumptions, quotas and deployment parameters/order. Explain how to validate the architecture in an Azure subscription, including bootstrap, readiness checks and rollback. Unverified feasibility must be visible, not implied as confirmed.

Address retrieval permissions and revocation, source deletion, prompt injection, least-privilege tools, sensitive telemetry, model/version policy and evaluations, human review, model outages and token cost; preserve manual case work when AI fails.

Explain capacity and recurring cost drivers from the stated workload; distinguish core/AI availability and latency. Map each durable store to retention, backups, restoration dependencies and proposed RTO/RPO. No fabricated prices, load results or recovery evidence.

Deliver all required Atlas artifacts with matching stable numbered diagrams/flow tables, official icon provenance, searchable unclipped PDF pages and documented inspection. Provide an executive decision summary, junior-friendly end-to-end walkthrough, glossary, detailed configuration tables and explicit open decisions. Structural validity alone is not deployment realism.

stages.title: Durable agent-led resolution across business systems
stages.requirements: Add customer-local agents that coordinate diagnostics, entitlement lookup and replacement-order requests through customer CRM/ERP APIs. External systems remain systems of record. Design for 10,000 workflows/day/customer, five tool operations per workflow on average, bursts of 20 workflow starts/second and up to 7 days awaiting human approval. Two US-hosted partner APIs use OAuth 2.0 and rate-limit independently; one lacks native idempotency. Read-only diagnostics may run automatically. Credits, replacements, entitlement changes and outgoing commitments require an authorized person to approve the exact action, target and version; approvals expire after 24 hours or any material change. Credentials stay customer-local. The model proposes tools, but a deterministic authorization/execution boundary enforces them. An API can time out after committing an order; a callback may be duplicated, late or out of order. A worker may crash between a remote action and local acknowledgment. Explain where execution state lives and how it survives deployment. Do not claim exactly-once external effects without a supported external contract. Human operators must reconcile uncertain outcomes and replay safely. Add event audit correlation without recording secrets or unrestricted prompts. Preserve Stage 1 isolation, manual case service and recovery commitments.
acceptance: Model workflow states, durable checkpoints, approval binding/expiry, tool allowlists and business authorization outside the model. Include successful and denied/expired approval paths in diagrams or explicit state tables.

Resolve timeout-after-commit, duplicate/out-of-order callbacks and worker crash windows through idempotency, reconciliation, bounded retries, dead-letter handling and compensating actions where possible; identify where a human must settle an uncertain effect.

Specify customer-local credentials, OAuth scopes/rotation, outbound destinations, rate-limit/backpressure behavior, dependency outages, workflow retention, deployment-version compatibility and recovery of in-flight work.
Show cumulative architecture changes, migration/rollback steps and test cases for permissions, external failure, cost/concurrency and recovery without regressing Stage 1 guarantees.

stages.title: Offline-capable field service and hybrid integration
stages.requirements: Add a dispatcher and mobile technician workflow: a service case creates a work order, reserves parts, schedules a qualified technician and captures job completion with evidence. Per customer, assume up to 2,000 technicians, 8,000 work orders/day and up to 8 hours disconnected. A technician sees only assigned work and the minimum required customer information. Mobile devices are managed but may be lost. Explain encrypted local storage, offline authorization expiration, logout/wipe limits and revalidation before sensitive server actions. A technician and dispatcher may edit the same work order while the device is offline; do not use last-write-wins for inventory, financial commitments or safety-relevant completion. Photos average 4 MB, up to 10 per order; upload resumes after interruption and scans untrusted content. Inventory and ERP remain customer-owned on premises, reachable through a constrained private hybrid integration. Two customers have overlapping RFC1918 address spaces; provider infrastructure must not accidentally route one to the other. Scheduling suggestions respect skills, service windows and travel constraints, but a human dispatcher commits the schedule. Do not claim a language model alone solves route optimization. Preserve the previous action approval and customer isolation rules.
acceptance: Describe offline data subsets, device identity, local encryption, authorization expiry/revocation limitations and deterministic sync conflict rules with duplicate submission and reassignment tests.

Trace case-to-order, parts reservation, suggested/approved dispatch, mobile sync and completion evidence paths with state ownership, concurrency controls, resumable upload/scanning and uncertain external outcomes.

Draw and explain customer-specific hybrid routes and DNS, egress restrictions and overlapping-address isolation; name platform/customer responsibilities, deployment prerequisites and hybrid outage behavior.

Update full deployment and capacity/cost/recovery plans for mobile, object storage, scheduling and hybrid integration. Document the incremental migration and prove earlier case and workflow requirements remain accounted for.

stages.title: Proactive equipment service at event-processing scale
stages.requirements: Add equipment telemetry that detects service issues and creates proposed cases/work orders for human approval. A largest customer has 100,000 devices, each sending a 1 KB event every 30 seconds, with a 10x burst for 5 minutes after reconnect. Events include device ID, sequence number, device timestamp and schema version. Device clocks drift and messages can arrive late, duplicated or in the wrong order. Keep raw telemetry 30 days and aggregates 13 months, all within the customer boundary and US residency. Explain device onboarding, per-device credentials/certificates, revocation and fleet updates separately from human SSO. A compromised device must not obtain business API or agent permissions. Use deterministic detection/aggregation before selectively invoking models; do not send each raw event to an LLM. An equipment fault should create at most one active proposed work item per defined incident window, subject to documented reconciliation limits. Separate ingestion, stream processing, business workflows and agent inference so a burst cannot starve existing case service. Plan replay and schema evolution, throughput partitions and quotas, poison events, consumer lag and failover backlog. No agent sends commands to physical equipment.
acceptance: Derive steady/burst ingress rate, bytes, retention and backlog assumptions from the fixture; map them to proposed service capacity, partitions/scaling, quotas and load-validation tests with cost drivers.
Explain device authentication/revocation, tenant isolation, schema validation, event-time/window policy, deduplication and replay checkpoints with concrete late/duplicate/poison-event failure tests.

Trace detection through authorized proposed work-item creation, including bounded AI calls, incident deduplication/reconciliation, human approval and protection of existing transactional latency during bursts.

Extend the cumulative platform/workload/recovery views and rollout plan. Include raw/aggregate data lifecycle, observability, backlog recovery and versioned migration without silently moving customer resources into a shared data plane.

stages.title: US multi-region recovery and dedicated-customer fleet operations
stages.requirements: Scale the provider to 200 dedicated customer subscriptions: 160 customers with 100–300 service staff and 40 with 600–1,200. Forty enterprise customers buy a premium recovery tier with two US regions. The other customers retain their earlier baseline. Premium core case/work-order service target is now 99.95% monthly availability, regional RTO 60 minutes and RPO 15 minutes; AI may degrade to manual operations. Select supported region/service combinations with documented dependencies, quota and model-capacity reservations rather than assuming every Azure service fails over identically. Customer case content, embeddings, workflow state and secrets remain isolated and US-resident. Shared management ingests only explicitly allowlisted operational/billing metadata. Explain normal and emergency provider access and how customer services continue if management, deployment tooling, identity dependencies or the primary region are unavailable. Roll out infrastructure/app/model changes through rings with version skew, customer maintenance windows, a canary, health gates and rollback; avoid one fleet-wide credential or policy mistake reaching all customers. Onboard subscriptions using repeatable automation, handle quotas and policy exceptions, rotate keys, detect drift and decommission with legal-hold-aware deletion evidence. Explain failover fencing, regional write ownership, DNS/routing changes, cross-region event duplication and in-flight business effect reconciliation. Include failback and a restore/recovery exercise with pass/fail measurements. A configuration proposal cannot prove the recovery targets. Provide a final complete reference design and a five-stage evolution summary, identifying simplifications retained, migrations, costs, operational burden and unresolved blockers to actual Azure deployment.
acceptance: Distinguish standard and premium placement and recovery contracts. Map every critical stateful dependency to replication/backup, RPO/RTO budget, region/tier support and failover/failback tests; expose any service that prevents the premium target.

Show regional traffic routing, single-writer/fencing rules, workflow/external-effect reconciliation and replay after failover, including split-brain prevention and manual operation when models are unavailable.

Describe implementable subscription onboarding, per-customer deployment identities, ring promotion, compatibility, rollback, drift, policy exceptions, keys, quotas, decommissioning and blast-radius limits. Shared management outage must not stop routine customer case work.

Show dedicated data and US residency through management telemetry, support, models, backups and failover. Include separate customer/region cost drivers and operational ownership at 200-customer scale, without implying a shared regional runtime is dedicated.

Deliver the complete cumulative architecture and evolution/migration summary. State which claims official evidence supports, which require deployment/load/recovery tests, and which prevent implementation sign-off. A junior developer, CTO, external enterprise architect and security architect must each receive actionable information rather than a generic service inventory.
